To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the spatial variability in grape yield was mainly influenced by the crop nutritional status, particularly with respect calcium and manganese contents in petioles; and (ii) the percentage of soil carbonate content was the main driver of grape quality.
soil fertility and crop nutrition play a key role in the spatial variability of grape yield and quality.
the zones of lowest grape yield coincided with areas with low crop nutrition and that the percentage of carbonates was the soil attribute that best correlated with grape quality parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a spatially explicit approach to vineyard management based on the spatial variability of soil properties and plant nutrition.
the spatial variability in grape yield, petiole mineral contents and grape quality, and the influence of different soil properties on these parameters.
the identification of key factors influencing grapevine spatial variability, and with the development of a strategy for vineyard management that is more efficient in the use of inputs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spatial variability of the vineyard is mainly driven by soil and crop nutritional factors, which are closely related to the vineyard topography.
the vineyard management should be based on the spatial variability of both grape yield and quality.
soil properties, crop nutrition and yield should be considered as key drivers for vineyard spatial variability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatial variability in grape yield is strongly influenced by the spatial variation in soil and crop nutritional characteristics, which could be used as a tool to improve the quality of the wine.
soil and crop properties are important factors that should be considered in site-specific vineyard practices.
soil properties and plant nutrient status are key drivers behind vine variability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
soil and crop nutrition are important drivers of grape yield and quality.
the spatial variability of grape quality and production is mainly related to the spatial variability in soil fertility and plant mineral nutrition.
it is possible to identify zones in which grape yield and grape quality are different, using yield maps.
